title: I Reported the Rideshare Cleanup Fee They Applied to an Empty Seat

parts.text: I rode six minutes from the clinic with a bottled water that never opened. The app charged a ninety-dollar cleanup for "bodily fluid on rear seat." I was thirty-five, nauseous from a shot, not from spilling. I had taken a photo of the empty back seat when I got out because the last driver had tried this on a friend. The photo showed dry gray fabric. I submitted it. The driver uploaded a photo of a stain in a different patterned seat. Then support froze my account for "dispute abuse."
parts.cliffhanger_hint: They froze me for showing a dry seat while he uploaded a different car.

social.video_title: Ninety dollars for a stain in another upholstery — Part 1/2
social.description: Six-minute clinic ride, unopened water, two fabrics. Then a freeze. Would you have photographed the seat?

parts.text: I emailed the pattern mismatch and the freeze. A specialist restored the account, removed the fee, and flagged the driver. I took a bus for a week anyway because trust is a muscle. The gray seat stays in my camera roll. Bodily fluid is a serious claim. It should match the car. My shot wore off. The water opened at home. The app still exists. So do patterns.

social.video_title: The specialist could see two different seats — Part 2/2
social.description: Fee gone, driver flagged, bus week as a palate cleanser. Was a freeze a stain?
